verdicts.reason: The reported batch t statistics and p-values are incompatible with a common residual degrees of freedom, even allowing for rounding.

The model F-test reports five numerator degrees of freedom even though the coefficient table shows only four estimable terms beyond the intercept.
The Batch_X and Inspector_2 t statistics and p-values cannot both come from the same residual degrees of freedom.
With singular.ok = TRUE, base R's lm.fit permits a rank-deficient fit and does not emit the displayed singularity warning.
The reported lack-of-fit F statistic and degrees of freedom imply a p-value above 0.05, contradicting the stated significance.
The reported lack-of-fit F statistic and degrees of freedom do not yield the printed p-value or support significance at 0.05.
The lack-of-fit F statistic and its two degrees of freedom do not yield the stated p-value.
The reported lack-of-fit F statistic is inconsistent with the ratio of the lack-of-fit and pure-error mean squares.
The lack-of-fit p-value is inconsistent with the stated F statistic and degrees of freedom.
The printed p-value does not match the lack-of-fit F statistic and the stated degrees of freedom.
The table places the lack-of-fit F statistic and p-value on the pure-error row, leaving the row for the test being interpreted blank.
Calling anova on a single Poisson GLM with a chi-square test does not append the displayed Pearson goodness-of-fit test.
The driver_age F statistic uses the pure-error mean square as its denominator, which is inconsistent with the ordinary regression F-test.
The displayed pchisq result does not match the supplied deviance and degrees of freedom.
The reported Pearson p-value does not match the upper chi-square tail for the stated statistic and degrees of freedom.
The lack-of-fit p-value does not match the F statistic and the lack-of-fit and pure-error degrees of freedom.
The marginal response summary cannot establish OLS unbiasedness or the shape of the slope t statistic's sampling distribution, and none of the options respects that limitation.
The summary supports a clear interpretation of skewness and robustness.
The summary and normality test do not establish that the sample mean has high sampling variance, and none of the options validly characterizes the estimators' sampling distributions.
The only option that recognizes the apparent right skew also makes an unsupported claim about how the mean and median compare under repeated sampling.
The summary supports one interpretation of skewness and its implications for robustness.
The summary supports one interpretation of skewness and its possible effect on confidence interval coverage.
None of the choices matches the relative likelihood in the requested direction, and the available value near one-half corresponds to the reverse comparison.
For the stated Bernoulli logistic model with three parameters, the printed AIC is inconsistent with the residual deviance.
The stated assumptions identify one exact sampling distribution for the slope estimator.
In this interacted model, the interaction estimates a difference between slopes fitted to disjoint groups, so its standard error cannot be smaller than the reference-group slope's standard error.
The logistic coefficient has one correct conditional interpretation.
